lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: counterexamples and why a proof fails
lessonRef.title: Concept model B: counterexamples and why a proof fails

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Compare these two examples. Find the step where they stop being the same.

items.prompt: Third side is 18. Find the midsegment.

steps: Midsegment is half the third side.
Both are supplementary to the same angle.
Angles supplementary to the same angle are equal.
workedSolution.answer: both supplementary to a common angle

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 26°. Find the measure of the alternate interior angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 36° and 46°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
In a parallelogram, one angle measures 36°. Find the consecutive angle.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 44. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 22, and it is parallel to the third side
88, and it is parallel to the third side
22, and it is perpendicular to the third side
44, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The two lines are parallel, forcing the angles to match.
Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so both have the same measure.
Vertical angles are congruent by definition.
The angles are congruent because they are opposite in position.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 112°. Find the measure of the corresponding angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 52° and 72°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: In a parallelogram, one angle measures 47°. Find the opposite angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 58. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 29, and it is perpendicular to the third side
116, and it is parallel to the third side
58, and it is parallel to the third side
29, and it is parallel to the third side
